issues.t: Drive electronics fail and the car won't move
issues.sym: A drivetrain warning on the dash, the car losing drive power, or the car refusing to go into drive. The 12-volt systems still work.
issues.why: The Electric Motor Electronics (EME) module converts battery power for the motor. It is the most common electronic failure on the i3.
issues.next: Have the car towed to a BMW dealer or EV specialist and have the high-voltage system scanned. Ask whether any open recall or warranty covers the module.

issues.t: Drive electronics can cut power while driving (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive power while driving, with a warning on the dash. Brakes and steering still work.
issues.why: A circuit board problem in the Electric Motor Electronics module can shut off high-voltage power.
issues.next: Check your VIN with BMW. Dealers replace the module free.

issues.t: Charging slows to half speed or stops
issues.sym: Home or public Level 2 charging takes about twice as long as before, or the car shows a charging fault.
issues.why: The on-board charging electronics (called KLE) can fail or be limited by a protective software update, which halves the charging rate.
issues.next: Note how long a full charge takes. Have a BMW dealer check the KLE and software; a failed unit must be replaced.

issues.t: Battery range drops with age
issues.sym: Fewer miles per charge than when new, especially in cold weather. Early 60 Ah cars may only manage about 55 to 65 miles at higher mileage.
issues.why: Lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over time and miles. Some early cars also had software-related battery faults.
issues.next: Get a battery state-of-health report before buying. The original battery warranty was 8 years or 100,000 miles, so check whether any coverage is left.

issues.t: Battery management module fault
issues.sym: Battery or drivetrain warning lights, sometimes with reduced power.
issues.why: The battery management electronics inside the high-voltage pack can develop faults, usually between 40,000 and 70,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the high-voltage system scanned by a BMW dealer or EV specialist. Software updates fix some faults.

issues.t: Range extender fuel system faults
issues.sym: A check engine light, a fuel door that won't open, or the range extender not starting when the battery runs low.
issues.why: Fuel injectors, oxygen sensors, fuel pump relays and the tank pressure sensor on the REx fail more often than expected. In the US the tank pressure sensor connector could corrode even when the engine is rarely used.
issues.next: Have the codes read. BMW released a tank pressure sensor with gold-plated connectors; ask whether yours has been updated.

issues.t: Fuel vent line can rub through and leak vapor (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell, though often there is no warning.
issues.why: The fuel tank vent line can rub against the main battery cable's sleeve and wear a hole, letting fuel vapor out.
issues.next: Check your VIN with BMW. Dealers inspect the line, replace it if needed and add a clip.

issues.t: Range extender engine fails after neglect
issues.sym: The REx won't start or struggles under load, overheats, or shows engine warnings when the battery gets low.
issues.why: The small 2-cylinder generator often sits unused for months. Stale fuel, seized fuel pumps, skipped yearly oil changes and hard sustained use all wear it out.
issues.next: Change the REx oil every year even if it rarely runs, keep fresh fuel in the small tank, and let the engine run now and then.

issues.t: Range extender engine mounts wear and shake
issues.sym: More vibration or buzzing in the cabin when the range extender is running.
issues.why: The rubber mounts holding the REx engine wear and develop play, often around 50,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected and replaced if worn.

issues.t: Motor mount brackets crack
issues.sym: A low buzzing from under the rear while charging, clunks when pulling away, or in some cases the car won't drive.
issues.why: Early cars used plastic brackets and bolts for the drive motor that could crack under repeated torque. BMW later switched to aluminium brackets.
issues.next: Have the motor mounts inspected and replaced with the updated parts.

issues.t: Whine or clunk from the rear drive motor
issues.sym: A faint whine that rises with speed, or a clunk from the rear when accelerating or slowing.
issues.why: Wear in the electric motor's bearings or the rear drive unit.
issues.next: Have it checked early. An independent EV shop may be able to repair the bearing instead of replacing the motor.

issues.t: DC fast charging won't start
issues.sym: The car refuses to begin a DC fast-charge session or stops right away, while slower charging may still work.
issues.why: A faulty charging control module or bent, corroded or damaged pins in the charge inlet.
issues.next: Look for damage or corrosion in the port, then have the charging system scanned. Replacing the inlet is a big job, so confirm the cause first.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not protect small unbelted drivers (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign.
issues.why: The driver airbag control software did not meet federal crash rules for small adults not wearing a seat belt.
issues.next: Always wear your seat belt, and have the free software update done at a BMW dealer.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not deploy properly (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; the problem only shows in a crash.
issues.why: A manufacturing error in the passenger front airbag module.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the airbag module replaced free if it is still open.

issues.t: Seat side airbags may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; the problem only shows in a crash.
issues.why: The igniters in the seat-mounted side airbags may fail to fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN with BMW; the airbag modules are replaced free.

issues.t: Portable charging cord can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: The supplied portable charger gets hot or smells of burning, though often there is no warning.
issues.why: Capacitors in the TurboCord portable charger can fail, creating a shock or fire risk.
issues.next: Stop using the portable cord and contact a BMW dealer for the free fix.

issues.t: Air conditioning or heat stops working
issues.sym: Warm air from the vents, weak heating in winter, or grinding from the A/C compressor.
issues.why: Early cars had software faults in the climate system. Some cars, including 2017 models, have had the electric A/C compressor fail and spread metal debris through the system.
issues.next: Have the climate system scanned for codes and updates first. If the compressor failed, the whole system must be flushed or parts replaced.

issues.t: Adaptive cruise control brakes suddenly or shuts off
issues.sym: With active cruise control on, the car slows hard for no reason, or the system switches itself off.
issues.why: The camera and radar can misread dips, bridges and bright sunlight, especially combined with strong regenerative braking.
issues.next: Stay ready to take over. Ask a dealer for software updates and to check sensor alignment.

issues.t: Center display freezes or reboots
issues.sym: The center screen freezes, restarts or stops responding.
issues.why: Software corruption in the display unit on pre-2017 cars.
issues.next: A dealer software update usually fixes it.

issues.t: Suspension joints and bushings wear and clunk
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, steering that feels off-center, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Steering swivel joints, upper strut mounts and rear trailing arm bushings are known weak spots, especially on rough city roads.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected and get an alignment after any repair.

issues.t: Brake rotors rust because they're rarely used
issues.sym: Grinding or scraping when braking, visible rust ridges on the rotors, or vibration.
issues.why: Regenerative braking does most of the stopping, so the friction brakes sit unused and corrode.
issues.next: Use the brakes firmly now and then. Have them inspected yearly and replace rusty rotors when needed.

issues.t: Narrow tires puncture easily
issues.sym: Frequent flat tires, sidewall bulges after potholes, or a hard time finding replacement tires.
issues.why: The i3 uses unusually narrow, tall tires on 19 or 20-inch wheels, and there's no spare.
issues.next: Check pressures often and carry the repair kit.
